LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_EnabledTip: Equip newly generated NPC combatants and let NPCs and prisoners use appropriate medical supplies. Existing pawns receive no free equipment.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_Training: Improve newly generated medics' Medical skill
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_TrainingTip: Apply a technology-scaled minimum Medical skill to newly generated medics. Existing world pawns keep their skills.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_OwnTip: Allow care for nearby group members. Self-treatment remains available.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_FriendlyTip: Provide nearby emergency assistance to allied factions.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_NeutralTip: Provide nearby emergency assistance to non-hostile strangers after comparable emergencies in their own group.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_PlayerTip: Allow nearby NPCs to help colonists in a life-threatening emergency, respecting medical-care restrictions.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_BoostsTip: Supply and allow eligible carriers to take combat boosters. Clinical pain and wound treatments remain separate, as do clinical epinephrine limits.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_TitleTip: Medical supplies and emergency behavior for NPC combatants and prisoners. Includes medic equipment, permitted patients, and combat-drug limits.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_ModeTip: Choose how much control More Injuries has over NPC treatment and survival decisions. Hover each menu choice for its behavior.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_Mode0Tip: Adds medical actions and ordinary travel to patients and supplies, without tactical repositioning, casualty extraction, medical withdrawal, or evacuation.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_Mode1Tip: Adds medical actions, nearby safer treatment positions, and local casualty extraction. Other mods retain retreat and off-map rescue decisions, except while a local extraction is committed.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_Mode2Tip: Also permits individual medical withdrawal and safe off-map evacuation of nearby downed faction members. Available treatment is considered first; casualty evacuation is deferred during immediate combat. Does not change group retreat decisions.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_EquipmentTip: Supply quantities, medic prevalence, rare scavenged equipment, and optional training for newly generated medics. Existing pawns receive no free equipment.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_SuppliesTip: Scale medical consumables, clinical reserves and booster reserves granted to newly generated NPCs. Reusable devices and sedatives are unchanged. Existing supplies count toward the kit.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_MedicsTip: Scale the proportion of newly generated combatants selected as medics. Zero stops selecting medics; ordinary personal supplies are controlled separately.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_ScavengingTip: Chance for a newly equipped NPC to carry an extra scavenged medical item. Allows rare equipment outside the usual technology-tier kit.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_CareTip: Choose which nearby non-hostile patients NPCs may assist. Self-treatment remains available independently of these flags.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_DrugsTip: Performance-drug provisioning and use, per-engagement dose limits, and separate intervals for performance and clinical drugs.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_SelectionTip: Choose booster supplies for newly generated NPCs. Existing provisioning only also blocks new clinical drug reserves. Existing items are preserved; use chance, dose limits and safety checks still apply.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_Selection0Tip: Choose performance drugs from the NPC technology-tier profile. More advanced factions can receive different drugs; this does not guarantee a dose.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_Selection1Tip: Use morphine for performance-drug provisioning. It reduces pain but can sedate, impair breathing and cause addiction; it is not equivalent to a stimulant.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_Selection2Tip: Add no new drugs to kits or scavenging, including clinical reserves and boosters. NPCs may still use permitted drugs already supplied by vanilla or another mod.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_PrevalenceTip: Scale the chance that newly generated NPCs receive a performance drug. Zero stops new performance-drug grants; existing supplies can still be used.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_UseChanceTip: Chance for an eligible carrier to use performance drugs during a combat engagement. Rolled once per engagement. Medical safety checks and dose limits still apply.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_MaximumTip: Maximum performance-drug doses per combat engagement. Zero prevents automatic performance use. Clinical epinephrine has a separate budget.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_PerformanceIntervalTip: Minimum time between performance-drug doses, including across engagements and saved games. 2,500 ticks equal one in-game hour. Zero removes this interval; other limits still apply.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_ClinicalIntervalTip: Minimum time between emergency epinephrine doses. Clinical pain care uses effect-based redosing and does not consume this interval or performance allowance. 2,500 ticks equal one in-game hour.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_PainCareTip: Use available safe analgesics for indicated pain relief and help nearby pawns downed by pain. Controls new pain-only reserves separately from combat boosters. Det?s wound treatments remain available for indicated healing or bleeding.
LanguageData.MI_NpcMedicine_PainThresholdTip: Fraction of each patient's actual pain-shock threshold at which preventive relief may begin. Default 50%. Existing sufficient analgesia prevents ineffective top-ups. Pain shock remains an emergency regardless of this setting.
